title: Descent to one complex dimension
html: By the descent theorem (jet prolongation), a two-complex-dimensional Descartes universe (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) with M = \mathbb{C}^2 descends to a one-complex-dimensional variety M_0. The stability of the Euler characteristic under descent and lifting (Euler characteristic stability) ensures that the descended universe retains \chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6. We may therefore study the Descartes universe using one-complex-dimensional varieties. The descent may continue to dimension zero (descent reduction to zero), where fibre data at a single point captures the entire quantum observable universe.
